questions.stem: What guiding idea summarises Sixth Normal Form (6NF)?
options: One attribute, one timeline, one table
One entity, one table, one key
Every determinant is a superkey
Every constraint is a domain or key constraint
One fact table, many dimension tables
questions.explanation: 6NF decomposes data so that each relation captures a single fact about a key, typically with explicit time validity: one attribute, one timeline, one table.

questions.stem: What is the condition for a table to be in Sixth Normal Form?
options: It is in BCNF and has no multi-valued dependencies
It is in 5NF and has been decomposed so that each relation captures a single fact about a key, typically with explicit time validity
It is in 3NF and all attributes are atomic
It is in 4NF and every join dependency is implied by keys
It is in DKNF and all constraints are structural
questions.explanation: A table is in 6NF when it is already in Fifth Normal Form and decomposed so each relation captures one fact about a key, usually with time validity.

questions.stem: What temporal problem does Sixth Normal Form solve for a loan whose interest rate and status change independently?
options: The loan can no longer be uniquely identified
The loan's attributes lose atomicity
Storing both attributes with effective dates in one table makes updates complex and overlapping intervals hard to manage
The interest rate becomes a multi-valued attribute
The status cannot be stored as a domain value
questions.explanation: When independently changing attributes share a table with effective dates, updates become complex and overlapping time intervals are difficult to manage, which 6NF resolves by giving each attribute its own timeline.

questions.stem: In the Sixth Normal Form loan example, what columns does the LoanInterestRate table contain?
options: LoanID, InterestRate, ProductType
LoanID, Amount, Status
ProductType, InterestRate
LoanID, InterestRate, EffectiveStart, EffectiveEnd
LoanID, InterestRate, TransactionTime
questions.explanation: The decomposition yields LoanInterestRate (LoanID, InterestRate, EffectiveStart, EffectiveEnd), so the interest rate evolves along its own timeline.

questions.stem: What typically makes up the primary key of a Sixth Normal Form table?
options: A surrogate integer alone
The attribute value itself
The business key alone
A hash of all columns
The business key combined with a validity period, such as LoanID and EffectiveStart
questions.explanation: In 6NF the primary key typically consists of the business key combined with a validity period, such as LoanID and EffectiveStart.

questions.stem: What is the difference between transaction-time and valid-time in bi-temporal modelling?
options: Transaction-time is when the record was stored in the system; valid-time is when the fact is true in the business world
Transaction-time is the loan origination date; valid-time is the repayment date
Transaction-time is the effective end date; valid-time is the effective start date
Transaction-time applies to OLTP; valid-time applies to OLAP
They are two names for the same timestamp
questions.explanation: Transaction-time records when a fact was stored in the system and valid-time records when it is true in the business world; storing both enables bi-temporal modelling for auditability and compliance.

questions.stem: Which modelling techniques are named as embracing Sixth Normal Form style fine-grained decomposition?
options: Star schema, snowflake schema and Unified Star Schema
Data Vault, Anchor Modelling and Focal Point Modelling
Hierarchical, network and object-oriented modelling
Document, key–value and graph databases
JSON schema, XML schema and API modelling
questions.explanation: 6NF is especially relevant in temporal modelling and ensemble techniques such as Data Vault, Anchor Modelling and Focal Point Modelling.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a benefit attributed to Sixth Normal Form?
options: Audit-grade temporal lineage
Clean separation of independently changing attributes
Fewer tables and simpler queries
Precise as-of queries and historical reconstruction
Independent attribute evolution
questions.explanation: 6NF increases table counts significantly and makes queries more complex; its benefits are auditability, separation of changing attributes and precise historical reconstruction.

questions.stem: For which scenarios is Sixth Normal Form said to be best suited?
options: General OLTP systems with simple CRUD operations
Static reference data that never changes
Read-heavy reporting dashboards
Regulatory, audit, pricing and contract scenarios
Key–value caching layers
questions.explanation: 6NF is best for regulatory, audit, pricing and contract scenarios where history and auditability are critical, and is often overkill for general OLTP.

questions.stem: How do many organisations apply Sixth Normal Form in practice?
options: They apply 6NF to every table in the schema
They avoid 6NF entirely in favour of star schemas
They apply 6NF only to dimension tables
They replace 6NF with DKNF
They normalise to 3NF or BCNF, then selectively apply 6NF-style histories only where needed
questions.explanation: Many shops normalise to 3NF/BCNF and then apply 6NF-style history tables surgically, only where independent attribute history is required.
